title: The Battlefield Can Become the Workshop
headline: What Is God Forming in You Through This Trial?
headline_sub: The Battlefield Can Become the Workshop
tagline: The fruit we pray for often becomes visible in the territory we would rather avoid.
seo_title: What Is God Forming in You Through Trials? (James 1:2-4) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Don't only ask God to get you out of the battle; ask who He is forming you to become in it. A devotional for men on James 1:2-4 and Romans 5:3-4.
verse_text: Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.

scriptures.text: Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.
….suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.

blocks.text: What if some of the places you keep asking God to remove are also places where God intends to form you?

items: Not because every difficulty was sent by God.
Not because evil becomes good.
Not because suffering should be romanticized.
But because God can form something in us through what we would have preferred never to experience.
We usually enter difficulty asking:
“How do I get out of this?”
“When will this be over?”
“When will they change?”
Those questions can be legitimate.
But discipleship teaches another question:

blocks.text: “Father, who are You forming me to become while I walk through this?”

items: The difficult coworker becomes an opportunity to practice patience.
The offense becomes territory for forgiveness.
The uncertainty becomes territory for trust.
The success becomes territory for humility.
The delay becomes territory for endurance.
The temptation becomes territory for self-control.
The battlefield has not disappeared.
But the battlefield can become the workshop.

sections.label: You Have Been Asking for the Fruit

items: We pray, “Lord, give me patience.”
“Give me self-control.”
“Help me love people better.”
But how do you practice patience without something that tries your patience?
How do you practice forgiveness without an offense?
The fruit we pray for often becomes visible in the territory we would rather avoid.
What happens to you and what is formed in you are not the same question.
God often gives enough light for obedience without enough light for control.
Don’t only ask, “When will this end?” Ask, “How do I follow Jesus here?”
Nothing that happened has to be wasted in the hands of God.
